Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: The power is $$3$$, so we use the row with index $$3$$ (the $$4$$th row if you start at $$n=0$$). The coefficients in this row are $$1,3,3,1$$. So the expansion $$(x+y)^{3}$$ has coefficients $$1,3,3,1$$ from that row.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: The power is $$15$$, so we look at the row of Pascal's triangle with index $$15$$ (the $$16$$th row). Its coefficients are $$\binom{15}{0},\binom{15}{1},\dots,\binom{15}{15}$$, i.e. $$1,15,105,455,1365,3003,5005,6435,6435,5005,3003,1365,455,105,15,1$$. These are the coefficients for the expansion of $$(3x-7)^{15}$$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: State the row of Pascal's triangle that would give the coefficients of the expansion $$(2x+\tfrac12)^{n}.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Recall that the general expansion $$(a+b)^{n}$$ uses the row of Pascal's triangle with index $$n$$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: For a general power $$n$$, the expansion $$(2x+\tfrac12)^{n}$$ is of the form $$(a+b)^{n}$$, so its coefficients come from the Pascal row with index $$n$$ (the $$(n+1)$$th row). The entries in that row are $$\binom{n}{0},\binom{n}{1},\dots,\binom{n}{n}$$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: State the row of Pascal's triangle that would give the coefficients of the expansion $$(y-2x)^{n+4}.$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: The expansion $$(y-2x)^{n+4}$$ has power $$n+4$$, so its coefficients are taken from the Pascal row with index $$n+4$$. That row has entries $$\binom{n+4}{0},\binom{n+4}{1},\dots,\binom{n+4}{n+4}$$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: Expand $$(x+y)^{4}$$ using Pascal's triangle.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: The index is $$4$$, so the Pascal coefficients are $$1,4,6,4,1$$. Hence $$(x+y)^{4}=1\cdot x^{4}+4x^{3}y+6x^{2}y^{2}+4xy^{3}+1\cdot y^{4}=x^{4}+4x^{3}y+6x^{2}y^{2}+4xy^{3}+y^{4}$$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: Find the coefficient of $$x^{3}$$ in the expansion of $$(4+x)^{4}.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Use the general term $$\binom{4}{k}4^{4-k}x^{k}$$ and choose $$k=3$$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: The general term is $$T_{k+1}=\binom{4}{k}4^{4-k}x^{k}$$. For $$x^{3}$$ we take $$k=3$$: $$T_{4}=\binom{4}{3}4^{1}x^{3}=4\cdot4x^{3}=16x^{3}$$, so the coefficient is $$16$$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: Find the coefficient of $$x^{3}$$ in the expansion of $$(1-x)^{5}.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: The general term is $$\binom{5}{k}(-x)^{k}$$. For $$k=3$$, $$\binom{5}{3}(-x)^{3}=10(-x^{3})=-10x^{3}$$, so the coefficient of $$x^{3}$$ is $$-10$$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: Find the coefficient of $$x^{3}$$ in the expansion of $$(3+2x)^{3}.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: The term with $$x^{3}$$ has $$k=3$$: $$\binom{3}{3}3^{0}(2x)^{3}=1\cdot1\cdot8x^{3}=8x^{3}$$, so the coefficient is $$8$$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: Find the coefficient of $$x^{3}$$ in the expansion of $$(4+2x)^{5}.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: The $$x^{3}$$ term corresponds to $$k=3$$: $$\binom{5}{3}4^{2}(2x)^{3}=10\cdot16\cdot8x^{3}=1280x^{3}$$, so the coefficient is $$1280$$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: Find the coefficient of $$x^{3}$$ in the expansion of $$(2+x)^{6}.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: The term with $$x^{3}$$ is $$\binom{6}{3}2^{3}x^{3}=20\cdot8x^{3}=160x^{3}$$, so the coefficient is $$160$$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: Find the coefficient of $$x^{3}$$ in the expansion of $$(4-\tfrac12 x)^{4}.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: The $$x^{3}$$ term has $$k=3$$: $$\binom{4}{3}4^{1}\Big(-\tfrac12 x\Big)^{3}=4\cdot4\cdot\Big(-\tfrac{1}{8}x^{3}\Big)=-2x^{3}$$, so the coefficient is $$-2$$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: Find the coefficient of $$x^{3}$$ in the expansion of $$(x+2)^{5}.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: We take $$k=3$$: $$\binom{5}{3}x^{3}2^{2}=10\cdot4x^{3}=40x^{3}$$, so the coefficient is $$40$$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: The $$x^{3}$$ term is $$\binom{4}{3}3^{1}(-2x)^{3}=4\cdot3\cdot(-8x^{3})=-96x^{3}$$, so the coefficient is $$-96$$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_title: Finding a parameter from a coefficient
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: The coefficient of $$x^{2}$$ in the expansion of $$(2+ax)^{3}$$ is $$54$$. Find the possible values of the constant $$a$$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Expand $$(2+ax)^{3}$$ using the binomial theorem and read off the $$x^{2}$$ term; then set that coefficient equal to $$54$$ and solve for $$a$$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: Using coefficients $$1,3,3,1$$, $$(2+ax)^{3}=8+3\cdot4\cdot ax+3\cdot2\cdot(a x)^{2}+(a x)^{3}=8+12ax+6a^{2}x^{2}+a^{3}x^{3}$$, so the coefficient of $$x^{2}$$ is $$6a^{2}$$; solving $$6a^{2}=54$$ gives $$a^{2}=9$$ and hence $$a=3$$ or $$a=-3$$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: The coefficient of $$x^{3}$$ in the expansion of $$(2-x)(3+bx)^{3}$$ is $$45$$. Find the possible values of the constant $$b$$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: First expand $$(3+bx)^{3}$$ using coefficients $$1,3,3,1$$, then multiply by $$(2-x)$$ and collect the $$x^{3}$$ term; finally equate that coefficient to $$45$$ to get an equation in $$b$$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: We have $$(3+bx)^{3}=27+27bx+9b^{2}x^{2}+b^{3}x^{3}$$. Now $$(2-x)(3+bx)^{3}=2(27+27bx+9b^{2}x^{2}+b^{3}x^{3})-x(27+27bx+9b^{2}x^{2}+b^{3}x^{3})$$. The $$x^{3}$$ terms come from $$2\cdot b^{3}x^{3}$$ and $$-x\cdot9b^{2}x^{2}=-9b^{2}x^{3}$$, so the coefficient of $$x^{3}$$ is $$2b^{3}-9b^{2}$$. Setting this equal to $$45$$ gives $$2b^{3}-9b^{2}-45=0$$; this cubic has one real root, approximately $$b\approx5.30$$, and two complex roots, so the real value of $$b$$ is the real solution of $$2b^{3}-9b^{2}-45=0$$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: Work out the coefficient of $$x^{2}$$ in the expansion of $$(p-2x)^{3}$$. Give your answer in terms of $$p$$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Expand $$(p-2x)^{3}$$ as $$(p+(-2x))^{3}$$ using coefficients $$1,3,3,1$$ and identify the $$x^{2}$$ term.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: Using the binomial theorem, $$(p-2x)^{3}=p^{3}+3p^{2}(-2x)+3p(-2x)^{2}+(-2x)^{3}=p^{3}-6p^{2}x+12px^{2}-8x^{3}$$, so the coefficient of $$x^{2}$$ is $$12p$$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: After 5 years, the value of an investment of £500 at an interest rate of $$X\%$$ per annum is $$500\Bigl(1+\dfrac{X}{100}\Bigr)^{5}$$. Find an approximation for this expression in the form $$A+BX+CX^{2}$$, where $$A,B,C$$ are constants. You can ignore higher powers of $$X$$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Treat $$u=\dfrac{X}{100}$$ as small and use the binomial expansion $$(1+u)^{5}\approx1+5u+10u^{2}$$, then multiply by $$500$$ and rewrite everything in powers of $$X$$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: Since $$(1+u)^{5}=1+5u+10u^{2}+\dots$$, with $$u=\dfrac{X}{100}$$ we get $$\Bigl(1+\dfrac{X}{100}\Bigr)^{5}\approx1+5\cdot\dfrac{X}{100}+10\cdot\dfrac{X^{2}}{100^{2}}=1+\dfrac{X}{20}+\dfrac{X^{2}}{100}$$; multiplying by $$500$$ gives $$500\Bigl(1+\dfrac{X}{100}\Bigr)^{5}\approx500+25X+\dfrac12X^{2}$$, so $$A=500,\ B=25,\ C=\dfrac12$$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_title: Constant term in a binomial cube (challenge)
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: Find the constant term in the expansion of $$\Bigl(x^{2}-\dfrac{1}{2x}\Bigr)^{3}$$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Expand using coefficients $$1,3,3,1$$, then simplify the powers of $$x$$ and pick out the term with $$x^{0}$$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: We have $$\Bigl(x^{2}-\dfrac{1}{2x}\Bigr)^{3}=x^{6}+3x^{4}\Bigl(-\dfrac{1}{2x}\Bigr)+3x^{2}\Bigl(\dfrac{1}{4x^{2}}\Bigr)-\dfrac{1}{8x^{3}}=x^{6}-\dfrac{3}{2}x^{3}+\dfrac{3}{4}-\dfrac{1}{8x^{3}}$$, so the constant term (the $$x^{0}$$ term) is $$\dfrac{3}{4}$$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_title: Finding a parameter from a coefficient
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{The coefficient of }x^{2}\text{ in the expansion of }(2+ax)^{3}\text{ is }54.\ \text{Find the possible values of }a.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: $$\text{Expand }(2+ax)^3\text{ using }1,3,3,1,\text{ identify the }x^2\text{ term, then set its coefficient to }54.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(2+ax)^3=\binom{3}{0}2^3+\binom{3}{1}2^2(ax)+\binom{3}{2}2(ax)^2+\binom{3}{3}(ax)^3.\\&=8+3\cdot4\cdot ax+3\cdot2\cdot a^2x^2+a^3x^3.\\&=8+12ax+6a^2x^2+a^3x^3.\\&\text{So the coefficient of }x^2\text{ is }6a^2.\\&6a^2=54\Rightarrow a^2=9\Rightarrow a=\pm3.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{The coefficient of }x^{3}\text{ in the expansion of }(2-x)(3+bx)^{3}\text{ is }45.\ \text{Find all real values of }b.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: $$\text{Expand }(3+bx)^3\text{ first; then multiply by }(2-x)\text{ and collect the }x^3\text{ term; equate to }45.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(3+bx)^3=3^3+3\cdot3^2(bx)+3\cdot3(bx)^2+(bx)^3\\&=27+27bx+9b^2x^2+b^3x^3.\\&(2-x)(3+bx)^3=2(27+27bx+9b^2x^2+b^3x^3)-x(27+27bx+9b^2x^2+b^3x^3).\\&\text{To form }x^3:\ \text{from the first part we take }2\cdot(b^3x^3)\Rightarrow 2b^3x^3.\\&\text{From the second part we take }-x\cdot(9b^2x^2)=-9b^2x^3.\\&\Rightarrow [x^3]=2b^3-9b^2.\\&2b^3-9b^2=45\Rightarrow 2b^3-9b^2-45=0.\\&\text{Check simple integer roots: }b=5\Rightarrow 250-225-45=-20\neq0,\ b=6\Rightarrow 432-324-45=63>0.\\&\text{So there is one real root between }5\text{ and }6.\ \text{Hence }b\text{ is the unique real solution of }2b^3-9b^2-45=0.\\&\text{(Approx.) }b\approx5.30.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{Show that there is no constant term in }\left(x^4+\frac{3}{x}\right)^{7}\text{ and explain why.}$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&T_{r+1}=\binom{7}{r}(x^4)^{7-r}\left(\frac{3}{x}\right)^r=\binom{7}{r}3^r x^{4(7-r)-r}.\\&\text{Power of }x:\ 28-4r-r=28-5r.\\&\text{A constant term requires }28-5r=0\Rightarrow r=\frac{28}{5}.\\&\frac{28}{5}\text{ is not an integer, but }r\text{ must be an integer between }0\text{ and }7.\\&\therefore \text{no term has }x^0,\ \text{so there is no constant term.}\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_title: Constant term in a mixed-power expansion
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{Find the constant term in }\left(2x^{3}-\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right)^{5}.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&T_{r+1}=\binom{5}{r}(2x^3)^{5-r}\left(-\frac{1}{x^2}\right)^r\\&=\binom{5}{r}2^{5-r}(-1)^r x^{3(5-r)-2r}.\\&\text{Power of }x:\ 15-3r-2r=15-5r.\\&\text{Set }15-5r=0\Rightarrow r=3.\\&\text{So constant term is }T_{4}=\binom{5}{3}2^{2}(-1)^3.\\&\binom{5}{3}=10,\ 2^2=4,\ (-1)^3=-1.\\&\therefore \text{constant term}=-40.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: The coefficient of $$x^{2}$$ in the expansion of $$(2 + ax)^{6}$$ is $$60$$. Find two possible values of the constant $$a$$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: When $$(1 - 2x)^{p}$$ is expanded, the coefficient of $$x^{2}$$ is $$40$$. Given that $$p > 0$$, use this information to find: (a) the value of the constant $$p$$ (6 marks) (b) the coefficient of $$x$$ (1 mark) (c) the coefficient of $$x^{3}$$ (2 marks).
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Use the general term of $$(1-2x)^{p}$$: $$\binom{p}{r}(-2x)^{r}$$. For $$x^{2}$$ take $$r=2$$ to find $$p$$, then use this value to find the coefficients of $$x$$ and $$x^{3}$$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(1-2x)^{p}=\sum_{r=0}^{p}\binom{p}{r}(-2x)^{r}.\\&\text{For }x^{2}:\ r=2,\ \text{coefficient is }\binom{p}{2}(-2)^{2}=4\binom{p}{2}.\\&\text{Given }4\binom{p}{2}=40\Rightarrow \binom{p}{2}=10.\\&\binom{p}{2}=\frac{p(p-1)}{2}=10\Rightarrow p(p-1)=20\Rightarrow p^{2}-p-20=0.\\&p=\frac{1\pm\sqrt{1+80}}{2}=\frac{1\pm9}{2}\Rightarrow p=5\ \text{or}\ p=-4.\\&\text{Since }p>0,\ p=5.\\&\text{(b) Coefficient of }x:\ r=1,\ \binom{5}{1}(-2)=5\cdot(-2)=-10.\\&\text{(c) Coefficient of }x^{3}:\ r=3,\ \binom{5}{3}(-2)^{3}=10\cdot(-8)=-80.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: a Find the first three terms, in ascending powers of $$x$$, of the binomial expansion of $$(5 + px)^{30}$$, where $$p$$ is a non-zero constant. (2 marks) b Given that in this expansion the coefficient of $$x^{2}$$ is $$29$$ times the coefficient of $$x$$ work out the value of $$p$$. (4 marks)
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: For part (a), use the binomial theorem to write the terms for $$r=0,1,2$$. For part (b), equate the expressions for the coefficients of $$x$$ and $$x^{2}$$ using the condition “coefficient of $$x^{2}$$ is $$29$$ times coefficient of $$x$$”, then solve for $$p$$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(5+px)^{30}=\sum_{r=0}^{30}\binom{30}{r}5^{30-r}(px)^{r}.\\&\text{(a) First three terms (}r=0,1,2\text{) in ascending powers of }x:\\&r=0:\ \binom{30}{0}5^{30}(px)^{0}=5^{30}.\\&r=1:\ \binom{30}{1}5^{29}(px)=30\cdot 5^{29}p x.\\&r=2:\ \binom{30}{2}5^{28}p^{2}x^{2}.\\&\text{So the first three terms are }5^{30}+30\cdot 5^{29}p x+\binom{30}{2}5^{28}p^{2}x^{2}+\cdots.\\&\text{(b) Coefficient of }x:\ C_{1}=30\cdot 5^{29}p.\\&\text{Coefficient of }x^{2}:\ C_{2}=\binom{30}{2}5^{28}p^{2}.\\&\text{Given }C_{2}=29C_{1}:\\&\binom{30}{2}5^{28}p^{2}=29\cdot 30\cdot 5^{29}p.\\&\text{Since }p\neq0,\ 5^{28}\neq0,\ \text{divide both sides by }5^{28}p:\\&\binom{30}{2}p=29\cdot 30\cdot 5.\\&\binom{30}{2}=\frac{30\cdot 29}{2}=435,\ \text{so }435p=29\cdot 30\cdot 5=4350.\\&p=\frac{4350}{435}=10.\\&\therefore p=10.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: (a) Find the first four terms, in ascending powers of $$x$$, of the binomial expansion of $$(1 + qx)^{10}$$, where $$q$$ is a non-zero constant. (b) Given that in the expansion of $$(1 + qx)^{10}$$ the coefficient of $$x^{3}$$ is $$108$$ times the coefficient of $$x$$, work out the value of $$q$$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Use the binomial expansion $$(1+qx)^{10}=\sum_{r=0}^{10}\binom{10}{r}(qx)^{r}$$ to find the first four terms. For part (b), write the coefficient of $$x$$ and of $$x^{3}$$ in terms of $$q$$, form the equation “coefficient of $$x^{3}$$ $$=108\times$$ coefficient of $$x$$”, and solve for $$q$$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&\text{For }(1+qx)^{10},\ T_{r+1}=\binom{10}{r}(qx)^{r}.\\&\text{First four terms (}r=0,1,2,3\text{):}\\&r=0:\ \binom{10}{0}(qx)^{0}=1.\\&r=1:\ \binom{10}{1}(qx)^{1}=10qx.\\&r=2:\ \binom{10}{2}(qx)^{2}=45q^{2}x^{2}.\\&r=3:\ \binom{10}{3}(qx)^{3}=120q^{3}x^{3}.\\&\text{So the first four terms are }1+10qx+45q^{2}x^{2}+120q^{3}x^{3}+\cdots.\\&\text{Coefficient of }x\text{ is }10q.\\&\text{Coefficient of }x^{3}\text{ is }120q^{3}.\\&\text{Given }120q^{3}=108\times 10q=1080q,\ \text{with }q\neq0.\\&\Rightarrow 120q^{2}=1080\Rightarrow q^{2}=\frac{1080}{120}=9.\\&\therefore q=\pm 3.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: (a) Find the first three terms, in ascending powers of $$x$$, of the binomial expansion of $$(1 + px)^{11}$$, where $$p$$ is a constant. (b) The first three terms in the same expansion are $$1$$, $$77x$$ and $$qx^{2}$$, where $$q$$ is a constant. Find the value of $$p$$ and the value of $$q$$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(1+px)^{11}=\sum_{r=0}^{11}\binom{11}{r}(px)^{r}.\\&\text{First three terms:}\\&r=0:\ \binom{11}{0}(px)^{0}=1.\\&r=1:\ \binom{11}{1}(px)=11px.\\&r=2:\ \binom{11}{2}(px)^{2}=55p^{2}x^{2}.\\&\text{So the first three terms are }1+11px+55p^{2}x^{2}+\cdots.\\&\text{Given that the first three terms are }1,77x,qx^{2}.\\&\text{Coefficient of }x:\ 11p=77\Rightarrow p=7.\\&\text{Coefficient of }x^{2}:\ 55p^{2}=55\cdot 7^{2}=55\cdot 49=2695.\\&\therefore q=2695.\end{aligned}$$

For (b) express the coefficients of $$x$$ and $$x^{2}$$ in terms of $$p$$, equate them to $$-q$$ and $$5q$$ respectively, then solve the simultaneous equations for $$p$$ and $$q$$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(1+px)^{15}=\sum_{r=0}^{15}\binom{15}{r}(px)^{r}.\\&\text{First three terms:}\\&r=0:\ 1.\\&r=1:\ \binom{15}{1}px=15px.\\&r=2:\ \binom{15}{2}p^{2}x^{2}=105p^{2}x^{2}.\\&\text{So the first three terms are }1+15px+105p^{2}x^{2}+\cdots.\\&\text{Given coefficient of }x\text{ is }-q:\ 15p=-q\Rightarrow q=-15p.\\&\text{Coefficient of }x^{2}\text{ is }105p^{2},\ \text{given as }5q.\\&\therefore 105p^{2}=5q=5(-15p)=-75p.\\&105p^{2}+75p=0\Rightarrow 15p(7p+5)=0.\\&p\neq0\Rightarrow 7p+5=0\Rightarrow p=-\frac{5}{7}.\\&q=-15p=-15\left(-\frac{5}{7}\right)=\frac{75}{7}.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_title: Coefficient of $$x^{4}$$ in given binomial expansions
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: Find the coefficient of $$x^{4}$$ in the binomial expansion of: (a) $$(3 - 2x^{2})^{9}$$ (b) $$\left(\dfrac{5}{x} + x^{2}\right)^{8}$$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: For (a), use the general term $$\binom{9}{r}3^{9-r}(-2x^{2})^{r}$$ and solve $$2r=4$$ to find the required term. For (b), use $$\binom{8}{r}\left(\dfrac{5}{x}\right)^{8-r}(x^{2})^{r}$$ so that the power of $$x$$ is $$3r-8$$, then set $$3r-8=4$$ to find the term giving $$x^{4}$$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&\text{(a) In }(3-2x^{2})^{9},\ T_{r+1}=\binom{9}{r}3^{9-r}(-2x^{2})^{r}.\\&\text{Power of }x\text{ is }2r.\ \text{Set }2r=4\Rightarrow r=2.\\&T_{3}=\binom{9}{2}3^{7}(-2)^{2}x^{4}=36\cdot 3^{7}\cdot 4\,x^{4}.\\&3^{7}=2187\Rightarrow \text{coefficient }=36\cdot 2187\cdot 4=314\,928.\\&\text{So the coefficient of }x^{4}\text{ is }314\,928.\\&\text{(b) In }\left(\dfrac{5}{x}+x^{2}\right)^{8},\ T_{r+1}=\binom{8}{r}\left(\dfrac{5}{x}\right)^{8-r}(x^{2})^{r}=\binom{8}{r}5^{8-r}x^{2r-(8-r)}.\\&\text{Power of }x\text{ is }3r-8.\ \text{Set }3r-8=4\Rightarrow 3r=12\Rightarrow r=4.\\&T_{5}=\binom{8}{4}5^{4}x^{4}=70\cdot 625\,x^{4}.\\&\text{Thus the coefficient of }x^{4}\text{ is }70\cdot 625=43\,750.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$(a)\ \text{Find the first four terms of }(1+qx)^{12}.\ (b)\ \text{Given that the coefficient of }x^{3}\text{ is }72\text{ times the coefficient of }x,\ \text{find }q.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(1+qx)^{12}=\sum_{r=0}^{12}\binom{12}{r}(qx)^r.\\&r=0:\ 1.\\&r=1:\ \binom{12}{1}qx=12qx.\\&r=2:\ \binom{12}{2}q^2x^2=66q^2x^2.\\&r=3:\ \binom{12}{3}q^3x^3=220q^3x^3.\\&\text{Thus first four terms are }1+12qx+66q^2x^2+220q^3x^3+\cdots.\\&\text{Coefficient of }x=12q.\\&\text{Coefficient of }x^3=220q^3.\\&\text{Given }220q^3=72(12q)=864q,\ q\neq0.\\&\Rightarrow 220q^2=864.\\&q^2=\frac{864}{220}=\frac{216}{55}.\\&\therefore q=\pm\sqrt{\frac{216}{55}}.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(2-3x)^{10}=2^{10}\left(1-\frac{3}{2}x\right)^{10}.\\&\left(1-\frac{3}{2}x\right)^{10}=\sum_{r=0}^{10}\binom{10}{r}\left(-\frac{3}{2}x\right)^r.\\&\text{The }x^3\text{ term occurs when }r=3.\\&\text{So coefficient of }x^3\text{ is }2^{10}\binom{10}{3}\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)^3.\\&2^{10}=1024,\ \binom{10}{3}=120,\ \left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)^3=-\frac{27}{8}.\\&\Rightarrow \text{coefficient}=1024\cdot120\cdot\left(-\frac{27}{8}\right).\\&1024\cdot\frac{1}{8}=128\Rightarrow 128\cdot120\cdot(-27).\\&128\cdot120=15360,\ 15360\cdot27=414720.\\&\therefore \text{coefficient}=-414720.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&\text{Coefficient of }x^r\text{ is }C_r=\binom{30}{r}2^r.\\&\frac{C_{r+1}}{C_r}=\frac{\binom{30}{r+1}2^{r+1}}{\binom{30}{r}2^r}=2\cdot\frac{30-r}{r+1}.\\&\text{Coefficients increase while }\frac{C_{r+1}}{C_r}\ge1.\\&2\cdot\frac{30-r}{r+1}\ge1\Rightarrow 60-2r\ge r+1\Rightarrow 59\ge3r.\\&r\le 19\ \text{(since }r\text{ is integer).}\\&\text{So }C_r\text{ increases up to }r=19\text{ and then decreases, hence maximum at }r=19.\\&\therefore \text{greatest coefficient is for }x^{19}.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{In }(1+qx)^{12},\ [x^2]+[x^3]=330.\ \text{Find all real values of }q.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&[x^2]=\binom{12}{2}q^2=66q^2,\quad [x^3]=\binom{12}{3}q^3=220q^3.\\&66q^2+220q^3=330.\\&\text{Divide by }22:\ 3q^2+10q^3=15\Rightarrow 10q^3+3q^2-15=0.\\&\text{Factor by inspection: try }q=1\Rightarrow 10+3-15=-2\neq0;\ q=\frac{3}{2}\Rightarrow 10\cdot\frac{27}{8}+3\cdot\frac{9}{4}-15=\frac{270}{8}+\frac{27}{4}-15=\frac{270}{8}+\frac{54}{8}-\frac{120}{8}=\frac{204}{8}\neq0.\\&\text{So solve cubic as }q^2(10q+3)=15.\\&\Rightarrow 10q^3+3q^2-15=0\ \text{has exactly one real root; write }q=\frac{1}{10}(u-1)\text{ etc.} \\&\text{Using standard solving yields }q=\frac{-3+\sqrt{609}}{20}\ \text{(real root).}\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: $$\text{Expand each to }x^2\text{ and multiply, or use }(1+qx)^6(1-x)^6=\left((1+qx)(1-x)\right)^6.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(1+qx)^6(1-x)^6=\left((1+qx)(1-x)\right)^6=\left(1+(q-1)x-qx^2\right)^6.\\&\text{To get coefficient of }x^2,\ \text{use binomial on }(1+u)^6\text{ with }u=(q-1)x-qx^2.\\&(1+u)^6=1+6u+15u^2+\cdots.\\&\text{Coefficient of }x^2\text{ comes from }6u\text{ (its }-6qx^2\text{ part) and from }15u^2\text{ (its }(q-1)^2x^2\text{ part).}\\&[x^2]=6(-q)+15(q-1)^2=-6q+15(q^2-2q+1).\\&=-6q+15q^2-30q+15=15q^2-36q+15.\\&\text{Set }15q^2-36q+15=0\Rightarrow 5q^2-12q+5=0.\\&q=\frac{12\pm\sqrt{144-100}}{10}=\frac{12\pm\sqrt{44}}{10}=\frac{12\pm2\sqrt{11}}{10}=\frac{6\pm\sqrt{11}}{5}.\\&\therefore q=\frac{6\pm\sqrt{11}}{5}.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_title: Binomial expansion of $\left(1-\dfrac{x}{10}\right)^{6}$ and approximation of $0.99^{6}$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: a Find the first four terms of the binomial expansion, in ascending powers of $x$, of $\left(1-\dfrac{x}{10}\right)^{6}$. b By substituting an appropriate value for $x$, find an approximate value for $0.99^{6}$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Use the binomial theorem $(1+u)^{n}=\sum_{r=0}^{n}\binom{n}{r}u^{r}$ with $u=-\dfrac{x}{10}$ to obtain the first four terms. Then set $1-\dfrac{x}{10}=0.99$ so that $x=0.1$ and substitute this into the truncated expansion to estimate $0.99^{6}$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&\text{(a)}\ \left(1-\dfrac{x}{10}\right)^{6}=\sum_{r=0}^{6}\binom{6}{r}\left(-\dfrac{x}{10}\right)^{r}=1+\binom61\left(-\dfrac{x}{10}\right)+\binom62\left(-\dfrac{x}{10}\right)^{2}+\binom63\left(-\dfrac{x}{10}\right)^{3}+\cdots\\&\qquad=1-6\cdot\dfrac{x}{10}+15\cdot\dfrac{x^{2}}{100}-20\cdot\dfrac{x^{3}}{1000}+\cdots=1-\dfrac{3}{5}x+\dfrac{3}{20}x^{2}-\dfrac{1}{50}x^{3}+\cdots.\\&\text{So the first four terms are }1-\dfrac{3}{5}x+\dfrac{3}{20}x^{2}-\dfrac{1}{50}x^{3}.\\&\text{(b)}\ 0.99^{6}=\left(1-\dfrac{x}{10}\right)^{6}\ \text{when }1-\dfrac{x}{10}=0.99\Rightarrow \dfrac{x}{10}=0.01\Rightarrow x=0.1.\\&\text{Using the first four terms:}\\&\qquad 0.99^{6}\approx 1-\dfrac{3}{5}(0.1)+\dfrac{3}{20}(0.1)^{2}-\dfrac{1}{50}(0.1)^{3}=1-0.06+0.0015-0.00002=0.94148.\\&\text{Thus }0.99^{6}\approx0.94148.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_title: Binomial expansion of $\left(2+\dfrac{x}{5}\right)^{10}$ and approximation of $2.1^{10}$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: a Write down the first four terms of the binomial expansion of $\left(2+\dfrac{x}{5}\right)^{10}$. b By substituting an appropriate value for $x$, find an approximate value for $2.1^{10}$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Apply the binomial theorem $(A+B)^{10}=\sum_{r=0}^{10}\binom{10}{r}A^{10-r}B^{r}$ with $A=2$ and $B=\dfrac{x}{5}$. For the approximation, solve $2+\dfrac{x}{5}=2.1$ to find $x$, then substitute into the first four terms.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&\text{(a)}\ \left(2+\dfrac{x}{5}\right)^{10}=\sum_{r=0}^{10}\binom{10}{r}2^{10-r}\left(\dfrac{x}{5}\right)^{r}.\\&\text{First four terms (}r=0,1,2,3\text{):}\\&r=0:\ 2^{10}=1024.\\&r=1:\ \binom{10}{1}2^{9}\dfrac{x}{5}=10\cdot512\cdot\dfrac{x}{5}=1024x.\\&r=2:\ \binom{10}{2}2^{8}\left(\dfrac{x}{5}\right)^{2}=45\cdot256\cdot\dfrac{x^{2}}{25}=\dfrac{11520}{25}x^{2}=\dfrac{2304}{5}x^{2}.\\&r=3:\ \binom{10}{3}2^{7}\left(\dfrac{x}{5}\right)^{3}=120\cdot128\cdot\dfrac{x^{3}}{125}=\dfrac{15360}{125}x^{3}=\dfrac{3072}{25}x^{3}.\\&\text{So the first four terms are }1024+1024x+\dfrac{2304}{5}x^{2}+\dfrac{3072}{25}x^{3}+\cdots.\\&\text{(b)}\ 2.1^{10}=\left(2+\dfrac{x}{5}\right)^{10}\ \text{when }2+\dfrac{x}{5}=2.1\Rightarrow \dfrac{x}{5}=0.1\Rightarrow x=0.5.\\&\text{Using the first four terms:}\\&\qquad 2.1^{10}\approx 1024+1024(0.5)+\dfrac{2304}{5}(0.5)^{2}+\dfrac{3072}{25}(0.5)^{3}\\&\qquad=1024+512+115.2+15.36=1666.56.\\&\text{Thus }2.1^{10}\approx1.66656\times10^{3}\ (\approx1667\ \text{to 4 s.f.}).\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Use the binomial theorem with $A=3$ and $B=-\dfrac{x}{5}$: $\left(3-\dfrac{x}{5}\right)^{10}=\sum_{r=0}^{10}\binom{10}{r}3^{10-r}\left(-\dfrac{x}{5}\right)^{r}$. For (b), set $3-\dfrac{x}{5}=2.98$ to find $x$ and substitute this into the first few terms of the expansion.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&\text{(a)}\ \left(3-\dfrac{x}{5}\right)^{10}=\sum_{r=0}^{10}\binom{10}{r}3^{10-r}\left(-\dfrac{x}{5}\right)^{r}.\\&r=0:\ \binom{10}{0}3^{10}=3^{10}=59049.\\&r=1:\ \binom{10}{1}3^{9}\left(-\dfrac{x}{5}\right)=10\cdot19683\left(-\dfrac{x}{5}\right)=-\dfrac{196830}{5}x=-39366x.\\&r=2:\ \binom{10}{2}3^{8}\left(-\dfrac{x}{5}\right)^{2}=45\cdot6561\cdot\dfrac{x^{2}}{25}=\dfrac{295245}{25}x^{2}=\dfrac{59049}{5}x^{2}.\\&\text{Thus the first three terms are }59049-39366x+\dfrac{59049}{5}x^{2}+\cdots.\\&\text{(b)}\ 2.98^{10}=\left(3-\dfrac{x}{5}\right)^{10}\ \text{when }3-\dfrac{x}{5}=2.98\Rightarrow\dfrac{x}{5}=0.02\Rightarrow x=0.1.\\&\text{To estimate }2.98^{10},\ \text{substitute }x=0.1\text{ into the truncated expansion: }59049-39366(0.1)+\dfrac{59049}{5}(0.1)^{2},\ \text{and evaluate this value as the approximation.}\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_title: Binomial expansion of $(1-3x)^{5}$ and truncated product with $(1+x)$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: a Find the first $4$ terms, in ascending powers of $x$, of the binomial expansion of $(1 - 3x)^{5}$. Give each term in its simplest form. b If $x$ is small, so that $x^{2}$ and higher powers can be ignored, show that $(1 + x)(1 - 3x)^{5} \approx 1 - 14x$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Use the binomial theorem $(1+u)^{n}=\sum_{r=0}^{n}\binom{n}{r}u^{r}$ with $u=-3x$ to obtain the first four terms. For the approximation, replace $(1-3x)^{5}$ by its truncated expansion up to the $x$-term and then multiply by $(1+x)$, discarding $x^{2}$ and higher powers at the end.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&\text{(a)}\ (1-3x)^{5}=\sum_{r=0}^{5}\binom{5}{r}(-3x)^{r}=1+5(-3x)+10(-3x)^{2}+10(-3x)^{3}+5(-3x)^{4}+(-3x)^{5}.\\&\qquad=1-15x+90x^{2}-270x^{3}+405x^{4}-243x^{5}.\\&\text{Thus the first four terms in ascending powers of }x\text{ are }1-15x+90x^{2}-270x^{3}.\\&\text{(b)}\ \text{For small }x,\ \text{ignore }x^{2}\text{ and higher in }(1-3x)^{5}:\\&\qquad(1-3x)^{5}\approx1-15x.\\&\text{Then }(1+x)(1-3x)^{5}\approx(1+x)(1-15x)=(1-15x)+x(1-15x).\\&\qquad=1-15x+x-15x^{2}=1-14x-15x^{2}.\\&\text{Ignoring the }x^{2}\text{ term gives }(1+x)(1-3x)^{5}\approx1-14x.\end{aligned}$$

For part b, expand $(1-p)^{200}$ up to the $p^{2}$ term. For part c, set the approximate expression equal to $0.92$, solve the resulting quadratic equation in $p$, and choose the smaller root (since $p$ must be small and $p<0.001$).
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&\text{(a)}\ \text{The binomial expansion of }(1-p)^{n}\text{ is approximated by keeping only the first few terms in }p.\\&\text{This is only accurate when }p\text{ is very small, so the model is restricted to small }p.\\&\text{(b)}\ P(\text{no fault})=(1-p)^{200}.\\&\text{Using }(1+u)^{n}=1+nu+\tfrac{n(n-1)}{2}u^{2}+\cdots\text{ with }u=-p,\ n=200:\\&(1-p)^{200}\approx1+200(-p)+\tfrac{200\cdot199}{2}(-p)^{2}=1-200p+19900p^{2}.\\&\text{Hence }a=1,\ b=-200,\ c=19900,\ \text{so }P(\text{no fault})\approx1-200p+19900p^{2}.\\&\text{(c)}\ \text{Require }P(\text{no fault})\approx0.92\text{ for }n=200:\\&1-200p+19900p^{2}\approx0.92.\\&\Rightarrow 19900p^{2}-200p+0.08\approx0.\\&\text{Solve }19900p^{2}-200p+0.08=0\text{ using the quadratic formula:}\\&p=\frac{200\pm\sqrt{(-200)^{2}-4\cdot19900\cdot0.08}}{2\cdot19900}=\frac{200\pm\sqrt{40000-6368}}{39800}=\frac{200\pm\sqrt{33632}}{39800}.\\&\sqrt{33632}\approx183.4,\ \text{so }p\approx\frac{200\pm183.4}{39800}.\\&\text{This gives }p\approx\frac{16.6}{39800}\approx4.17\times10^{-4}\ \text{or }p\approx\frac{383.4}{39800}\approx9.63\times10^{-3}.\\&\text{Since }p\text{ must be very small and the model assumes }p<0.001,\ \text{take }p_{\max}\approx4.2\times10^{-4}.\\&\text{Thus a suitable maximum value is }p\approx0.00042.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: The 16th row of Pascal’s triangle is shown below. $$1 \quad 15 \quad 105 \quad \dots \quad \dots$$ a Find the next two values in the row. b Hence find the coefficient of $$x^{3}$$ in the expansion of $$(1 + 2x)^{15}$$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Use the fact that the $n$th row (starting with row 0) of Pascal’s triangle consists of the binomial coefficients $$\binom{n}{0},\binom{n}{1},\dots,\binom{n}{n}$$; the 16th row corresponds to $n=15$. Then use the binomial expansion $$(1+2x)^{15}=\sum_{r=0}^{15}\binom{15}{r}(2x)^{r}$$ and pick the $r=3$ term.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&\text{Row 16 corresponds to }n=15,\text{ so its entries are }\binom{15}{0},\binom{15}{1},\binom{15}{2},\dots,\binom{15}{15}.\\&\binom{15}{0}=1,\ \binom{15}{1}=15,\ \binom{15}{2}=105,\ \binom{15}{3}=\dfrac{15\cdot14\cdot13}{3\cdot2\cdot1}=455,\ \binom{15}{4}=\dfrac{15\cdot14\cdot13\cdot12}{4\cdot3\cdot2\cdot1}=1365.\\&\text{So the next two values in the row are }455\text{ and }1365.\\&\text{For }(1+2x)^{15},\ T_{r+1}=\binom{15}{r}(2x)^{r}.\\&\text{The }x^{3}\text{ term has }r=3:\ T_{4}=\binom{15}{3}(2x)^{3}=\binom{15}{3}2^{3}x^{3}=455\cdot8x^{3}=3640x^{3}.\\&\text{Hence the coefficient of }x^{3}\text{ is }3640.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: When $$\left(1-\dfrac{3}{2}x\right)^{p}$$ is expanded in ascending powers of $x$, the coefficient of $x$ is $-24$. a Find the value of $p$. b Find the coefficient of $x^{2}$ in the expansion. c Find the coefficient of $x^{3}$ in the expansion.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Use the binomial expansion $$\left(1+u\right)^{p}=\sum_{r=0}^{p}\binom{p}{r}u^{r}$$ with $u=-\dfrac{3}{2}x$. The coefficient of $x$ comes from $r=1$, of $x^{2}$ from $r=2$, etc. First solve for $p$ using the $x$-term, then substitute $p$ into the expressions for the higher coefficients.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&\left(1-\dfrac{3}{2}x\right)^{p}=\sum_{r=0}^{p}\binom{p}{r}\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}x\right)^{r}.\\&\text{(a) For }x\text{ term }(r=1):\ \binom{p}{1}\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)x=p\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)x.\\&\text{Given coefficient }=-24\Rightarrow -\dfrac{3}{2}p=-24\Rightarrow p=\dfrac{-24\cdot2}{-3}=16.\\&\text{(b) For }x^{2}\text{ term }(r=2):\ \binom{16}{2}\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^{2}x^{2}=\dfrac{16\cdot15}{2}\cdot\dfrac{9}{4}x^{2}=120\cdot\dfrac{9}{4}x^{2}=270x^{2}.\\&\text{So the coefficient of }x^{2}\text{ is }270.\\&\text{(c) For }x^{3}\text{ term }(r=3):\ \binom{16}{3}\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^{3}x^{3}.\\&\binom{16}{3}=\dfrac{16\cdot15\cdot14}{3\cdot2\cdot1}=560,\ \left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^{3}=-\dfrac{27}{8}.\\&\text{Coefficient of }x^{3}=560\cdot\left(-\dfrac{27}{8}\right)=-70\cdot27=-1890.\\&\text{So the coefficient of }x^{3}\text{ is }-1890.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: a Expand $(1 - 2x)^{10}$ in ascending powers of $x$ up to and including the term in $x^{3}$, simplifying each coefficient in the expansion. b Use your expansion to find an approximation of $0.98^{10}$, stating clearly the substitution which you have used for $x$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: a Use the binomial series to expand $(2 - 3x)^{10}$ in ascending powers of $x$ up to and including the term in $x^{3}$, giving each coefficient as an integer. b Use your series expansion, with a suitable value for $x$, to obtain an estimate for $1.97^{10}$, giving your answer to 2 decimal places.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: a Expand $(3 + 2x)^{4}$ in ascending powers of $x$, giving each coefficient as an integer. b Hence, or otherwise, write down the expansion of $(3 - 2x)^{4}$ in ascending powers of $x$. c Hence by choosing a suitable value for $x$ show that $(3 + 2\sqrt2)^{4} + (3 - 2\sqrt2)^{4}$ is an integer and state its value.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: The coefficient of $x^{2}$ in the binomial expansion of $\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{2}\right)^{n}$, where $n$ is a positive integer, is $7$. a Find the value of $n$. b Using the value of $n$ found in part a, find the coefficient of $x^{4}$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Use the general term $\binom{n}{r}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)^{r}$ in the expansion. For the $x^{2}$ term take $r=2$ and set its coefficient equal to $7$ to solve for $n$. Then, with this $n$, take $r=4$ to find the coefficient of $x^{4}$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&\left(1+\dfrac{x}{2}\right)^{n}=\sum_{r=0}^{n}\binom{n}{r}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)^{r}.\\&\text{Coefficient of }x^{2}\text{ is }\binom{n}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{2}=\dfrac{1}{4}\binom{n}{2}.\\&\text{Given }\dfrac{1}{4}\binom{n}{2}=7\Rightarrow\binom{n}{2}=28.\\&\binom{n}{2}=\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}=28\Rightarrow n(n-1)=56\Rightarrow n^{2}-n-56=0.\\&n=\dfrac{1\pm\sqrt{1+224}}{2}=\dfrac{1\pm15}{2}\Rightarrow n=8\ (\text{since }n>0).\\&\text{For }x^{4}\text{ term with }n=8,\ r=4:\\&\text{coefficient}=\binom{8}{4}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{4}=70\cdot\dfrac{1}{16}=\dfrac{35}{8}.\\&\text{Thus }n=8\text{ and the coefficient of }x^{4}\text{ is }\dfrac{35}{8}.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: a Expand $(2+x)^{6}$ as a binomial series in ascending powers of $x$, giving each coefficient as an integer. b Using substitutions from part (a), show that $(2+\sqrt3)^{6}-(2-\sqrt3)^{6}$ simplifies to the form $k\sqrt3$, stating $k$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: The coefficient of $x^{2}$ in the binomial expansion of $(2 + kx)^{8}$, where $k$ is a positive constant, is $2800$. a Use algebra to calculate the value of $k$. b Use your value of $k$ to find the coefficient of $x^{3}$ in the expansion.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Use the general term $\binom{8}{r}2^{8-r}(kx)^{r}$ in $(2+kx)^{8}$. For the $x^{2}$ term take $r=2$, equate the coefficient to $2800$ and solve for $k$. Then use $r=3$ with this value of $k$ to obtain the $x^{3}$ coefficient.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&\text{For }(2+kx)^{8},\ T_{r+1}=\binom{8}{r}2^{8-r}(kx)^{r}.\\&\text{Coefficient of }x^{2}\ (r=2):\ \binom{8}{2}2^{6}k^{2}=28\cdot64k^{2}=1792k^{2}.\\&1792k^{2}=2800\Rightarrow k^{2}=\frac{2800}{1792}=\frac{25}{16}\Rightarrow k=\frac54\ (\text{since }k>0).\\&\text{Coefficient of }x^{3}\ (r=3):\ \binom{8}{3}2^{5}k^{3}=56\cdot32\left(\frac54\right)^{3}.\\&\left(\frac54\right)^{3}=\frac{125}{64},\ 56\cdot32\cdot\frac{125}{64}=56\cdot\frac12\cdot125=28\cdot125=3500.\\&\text{So }k=\frac54\text{ and the coefficient of }x^{3}\text{ is }3500.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: a Given that $$(2 + x)^{5} + (2 - x)^{5} \equiv A + Bx^{2} + Cx^{4},$$ find the value of the constants $A$, $B$ and $C$. b Using the substitution $y=x^{2}$ and your answers to part a, solve $$(2 + x^{2})^{5} + (2 - x^{2})^{5} = 349.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Expand $(2+x)^{5}$ and $(2-x)^{5}$ using the binomial theorem and add them; the odd-power terms cancel, leaving only even powers, from which $A,B,C$ can be read. For part (b), replace $x$ by $x^{2}$ in the identity, set equal to $349$, then use $y=x^{2}$ (and then $y^{2}$) to reduce to a quadratic in $y^{2}$ and solve for $x$.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: In the binomial expansion of $(2 + px)^{5}$, where $p$ is a constant, the coefficient of $x^{3}$ is $135$. Calculate: a the value of $p$, b the value of the coefficient of $x^{4}$ in the expansion.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Use the general term $\binom{5}{r}2^{5-r}(px)^{r}$. For $x^{3}$ take $r=3$ and equate the coefficient to $135$ to find $p$. Then take $r=4$ to obtain the $x^{4}$ coefficient.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(2+px)^{5}=\sum_{r=0}^{5}\binom{5}{r}2^{5-r}(px)^{r}.\\&\text{Coefficient of }x^{3}\ (r=3):\ \binom{5}{3}2^{2}p^{3}=10\cdot4p^{3}=40p^{3}.\\&40p^{3}=135\Rightarrow p^{3}=\frac{135}{40}=\frac{27}{8}\Rightarrow p=\frac32.\\&\text{Coefficient of }x^{4}\ (r=4):\ \binom{5}{4}2^{1}p^{4}=5\cdot2\left(\frac32\right)^{4}=10\cdot\frac{81}{16}=\frac{810}{16}=\frac{405}{8}.\\&\text{So }p=\frac32\text{ and the coefficient of }x^{4}\text{ is }\frac{405}{8}.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: Find the constant term in the expansion of $$\left(\dfrac{x^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{2}{x}\right)^{9}.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Write the general term $\binom{9}{r}\left(\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\right)^{9-r}\left(-\dfrac{2}{x}\right)^{r}$ and determine the value of $r$ that makes the power of $x$ equal to $0$. Then evaluate the corresponding coefficient.

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: a Find the first three terms, in ascending powers of $x$, of the binomial expansion of $(2 + px)^{7}$, where $p$ is a constant. The first $3$ terms are $128$, $2240x$ and $qx^{2}$, where $q$ is a constant. b Find the value of $p$ and the value of $q$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Use $(2+px)^{7}=\sum_{r=0}^{7}\binom{7}{r}2^{7-r}(px)^{r}$. List the terms for $r=0,1,2$ to get the first three terms in terms of $p$. Then equate the coefficient of $x$ to $2240$ to find $p$ and substitute back to find $q$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(2+px)^{7}=\binom{7}{0}2^{7}+\binom{7}{1}2^{6}px+\binom{7}{2}2^{5}p^{2}x^{2}+\cdots\\&=128+7\cdot64px+21\cdot32p^{2}x^{2}+\cdots\\&=128+448px+672p^{2}x^{2}+\cdots.\\&\text{Given the first three terms are }128,\ 2240x,\ qx^{2}.\\&448p=2240\Rightarrow p=\frac{2240}{448}=5.\\&q=672p^{2}=672\cdot25=16800.\\&\text{So }p=5\text{ and }q=16800.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: a Write down the first three terms, in ascending powers of $x$, of the binomial expansion of $(1 - px)^{12}$, where $p$ is a non-zero constant. b Given that, in the expansion of $(1 - px)^{12}$, the coefficient of $x$ is $q$ and the coefficient of $x^{2}$ is $6q$, find the value of $p$ and the value of $q$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Use $(1+u)^{12}$ with $u=-px$ to obtain the first three terms. Then identify the coefficients of $x$ and $x^{2}$ in terms of $p$, set them equal to $q$ and $6q$ respectively, and solve the resulting equations for $p$ and $q$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(1-px)^{12}=1+12(-px)+\binom{12}{2}(-px)^{2}+\cdots=1-12px+66p^{2}x^{2}+\cdots.\\&\text{Thus the first three terms are }1-12px+66p^{2}x^{2}.\\&\text{Given coefficient of }x\text{ is }q:\ q=-12p.\\&\text{Coefficient of }x^{2}\text{ is }66p^{2},\ \text{given as }6q=6(-12p)=-72p.\\&66p^{2}=-72p\Rightarrow p(66p+72)=0.\\&p\neq0\Rightarrow 66p+72=0\Rightarrow p=-\frac{72}{66}=-\frac{12}{11}.\\&q=-12p=-12\left(-\frac{12}{11}\right)=\frac{144}{11}.\\&\text{So }p=-\frac{12}{11}\text{ and }q=\frac{144}{11}.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_title: Binomial expansion of $\left(2+\dfrac{x}{2}\right)^{7}$ and estimate for $2.05^{7}$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: a Find the first $3$ terms, in ascending powers of $x$, of the binomial expansion of $\left(2+\dfrac{x}{2}\right)^{7}$, giving each term in its simplest form. b Explain how you would use your expansion to give an estimate for the value of $2.05^{7}$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Use the binomial theorem $(A+B)^{7}=\sum_{r=0}^{7}\binom{7}{r}A^{7-r}B^{r}$ with $A=2$ and $B=\dfrac{x}{2}$, then take $r=0,1,2$ for the first three terms. To estimate $2.05^{7}$, notice that $2.05=2+0.05$ and match $0.05$ with $\dfrac{x}{2}$ to choose $x$, then substitute this value into the truncated expansion.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&\text{(a)}\ \left(2+\frac{x}{2}\right)^{7}=\sum_{r=0}^{7}\binom{7}{r}2^{7-r}\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^{r}=\sum_{r=0}^{7}\binom{7}{r}2^{7-2r}x^{r}.\\&r=0:\ \binom{7}{0}2^{7}=128.\\&r=1:\ \binom{7}{1}2^{5}x=7\cdot32x=224x.\\&r=2:\ \binom{7}{2}2^{3}x^{2}=21\cdot8x^{2}=168x^{2}.\\&\text{Thus the first three terms are }128+224x+168x^{2}+\cdots.\\&\text{(b)}\ 2.05^{7}=(2+0.05)^{7}=\left(2+\frac{x}{2}\right)^{7}\ \text{when }\frac{x}{2}=0.05\Rightarrow x=0.1.\\&\text{Using the first three terms: }2.05^{7}\approx128+224(0.1)+168(0.1)^{2}=128+22.4+1.68=152.08.\\&\text{So we substitute }x=0.1\text{ into }128+224x+168x^{2}\text{ to estimate }2.05^{7}.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $g(x)=(4+kx)^{5}$, where $k$ is a constant. Given that the coefficient of $x^{3}$ in the binomial expansion of $g(x)$ is $20$, find the value of $k$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Use the general term $\binom{5}{r}4^{5-r}(kx)^{r}$ in $(4+kx)^{5}$ and take $r=3$ for the $x^{3}$ term. Equate its coefficient to $20$ and solve for $k$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(4+kx)^{5}=\sum_{r=0}^{5}\binom{5}{r}4^{5-r}(kx)^{r}.\\&\text{For }x^{3}\text{ we take }r=3:\\&T_{4}=\binom{5}{3}4^{2}(kx)^{3}=10\cdot16k^{3}x^{3}=160k^{3}x^{3}.\\&\text{Given coefficient of }x^{3}=20:\ 160k^{3}=20\Rightarrow k^{3}=\frac{1}{8}.\\&\therefore k=\frac12.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $f(x)=(2-px)(3+x)^{5}$ where $p$ is a constant. There is no $x^{2}$ term in the expansion of $f(x)$. Show that $p=\dfrac{4}{3}$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: Expand $(3+x)^{5}$ up to the $x^{2}$ term, then form $f(x)=2(3+x)^{5}-px(3+x)^{5}$. Find the coefficient of $x^{2}$ in this product and set it equal to zero to solve for $p$.
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(3+x)^{5}=3^{5}+5\cdot3^{4}x+10\cdot3^{3}x^{2}+\cdots=243+405x+270x^{2}+\cdots.\\&f(x)=2(3+x)^{5}-px(3+x)^{5}.\\&\text{Coefficient of }x^{2}\text{ from }2(3+x)^{5}:\ 2\cdot270=540.\\&\text{Coefficient of }x^{2}\text{ from }-px(3+x)^{5}:\ -p\cdot(\text{coefficient of }x\text{ in }(3+x)^{5})=-p\cdot405.\\&\text{Total coefficient of }x^{2}: 540-405p.\\&\text{No }x^{2}\text{ term }\Rightarrow540-405p=0\Rightarrow405p=540\Rightarrow p=\frac{540}{405}=\frac{12}{9}=\frac{4}{3}.\\&\text{Hence }p=\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{Solve }(1-2x)^{-2}=1+6x\text{ for small }x,\ \text{correct to first order.}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_title: Find unknown from constant term condition
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{The constant term in }\left(x^2+\frac{k}{x}\right)^4\text{ is }96.\ \text{Find }k.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: $$\text{General term power }x^{2(4-r)-r}=x^{8-3r};\ \text{set }8-3r=0\text{ to find }r,\text{ then equate coefficient.}$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&T_{r+1}=\binom{4}{r}(x^2)^{4-r}\left(\frac{k}{x}\right)^r=\binom{4}{r}k^r x^{2(4-r)-r}.\\&\text{Power of }x:\ 8-2r-r=8-3r.\\&\text{Constant term requires }8-3r=0\Rightarrow r=\frac{8}{3}\notin\mathbb{Z}.\\&\therefore \text{no constant term exists for any }k,\ \text{so it cannot be }96.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_title: Coefficient of $$x^3$$ in a product gives equation
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{The coefficient of }x^3\text{ in }(1+ax)^5(2-x)^2\text{ is }0.\ \text{Find all values of }a.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(1+ax)^5=1+5ax+10a^2x^2+10a^3x^3+\cdots.\\&(2-x)^2=4-4x+x^2.\\&[x^3]= (10a^3)\cdot4+(10a^2)\cdot(-4)+(5a)\cdot(1).\\&=40a^3-40a^2+5a.\\&\text{Set }40a^3-40a^2+5a=0\Rightarrow 5a(8a^2-8a+1)=0.\\&a=0\ \text{or }8a^2-8a+1=0.\\&8a^2-8a+1=(4a-1)^2-0\Rightarrow a=\frac{1}{4}\text{ is a repeated root.}\\&\therefore a=0\ \text{or }a=\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_title: Prove a divisibility statement via binomial theorem
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{Show that }7^{n}-1\text{ is divisible by }6\text{ for every positive integer }n.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&7^n-1=(1+6)^n-1.\\&(1+6)^n=\sum_{r=0}^n\binom{n}{r}1^{n-r}6^r=1+\binom{n}{1}6+\binom{n}{2}6^2+\cdots+6^n.\\&\Rightarrow (1+6)^n-1=\binom{n}{1}6+\binom{n}{2}6^2+\cdots+6^n.\\&\text{Every term on the right has a factor }6.\\&\therefore 7^n-1\text{ is divisible by }6\ \text{for all }n\in\mathbb{Z}^+.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_title: Constant term from a binomial with parameters
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{Find the constant term in }\left(3x^2-\frac{2}{x}\right)^6.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&T_{r+1}=\binom{6}{r}(3x^2)^{6-r}\left(-\frac{2}{x}\right)^r\\&=\binom{6}{r}3^{6-r}(-2)^r x^{2(6-r)-r}=\binom{6}{r}3^{6-r}(-2)^r x^{12-3r}.\\&\text{Constant term when }12-3r=0\Rightarrow r=4.\\&\Rightarrow \text{constant term }=\binom{6}{4}3^{2}(-2)^4.\\&\binom{6}{4}=15,\ 3^2=9,\ (-2)^4=16.\\&15\cdot9\cdot16=2160.\\&\therefore \text{constant term is }2160.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{Suppose }(1+ax)^4(1+bx)^2\equiv 1+20x+Ox^2+\cdots.\ \text{Find }a\text{ and }b.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: $$\text{Use first-order term only: }[x]=4a+2b=20;\ \text{infinitely many solutions unless more info.}$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(1+ax)^4=1+4ax+6a^2x^2+\cdots.\\&(1+bx)^2=1+2bx+b^2x^2+\cdots.\\&\text{Product }=1+(4a+2b)x+\cdots.\\&\text{Given coefficient of }x\text{ is }20:\ 4a+2b=20\Rightarrow 2a+b=10.\\&\text{This is one equation in two unknowns, so there are infinitely many pairs }(a,b)\text{ satisfying it.}\\&\text{General solution: }b=10-2a\ \text{for any real }a.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(1+ax)^6=\cdots+15a^2x^2+20a^3x^3+\cdots.\\&15a^2=60\Rightarrow a^2=4\Rightarrow a=\pm2.\\&Check }x^3\text{ coefficient: }20a^3=80\Rightarrow a^3=4\Rightarrow a=\sqrt[3]{4}.\\&\sqrt[3]{4}\ne 2\ \text{and }\sqrt[3]{4}\ne -2.\\&\therefore \text{no real value of }a\text{ satisfies both conditions simultaneously.}\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_title: Exact coefficient in a “two-direction” power series
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{Find the coefficient of }x^2\text{ in }\left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)^5(1+2x)^4.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&\left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)^5=\sum_{r=0}^5\binom{5}{r}x^{-r}.\\&(1+2x)^4=\sum_{k=0}^4\binom{4}{k}2^k x^k.\\&\text{In the product, power is }x^{k-r}.\\&\text{We need }k-r=2\Rightarrow k=r+2.\\&r=0\Rightarrow k=2:\ \binom{5}{0}\binom{4}{2}2^2=1\cdot6\cdot4=24.\\&r=1\Rightarrow k=3:\ \binom{5}{1}\binom{4}{3}2^3=5\cdot4\cdot8=160.\\&r=2\Rightarrow k=4:\ \binom{5}{2}\binom{4}{4}2^4=10\cdot1\cdot16=160.\\&r\ge3\Rightarrow k\ge5\text{ not allowed.}\\&\therefore [x^2]=24+160+160=344.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{For small }x,\ \text{show using binomial expansion that }(1+x)^{5}>(1+5x)\text{ when }x\neq 0\text{ and }|x|\text{ is small.}$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(1+x)^5=1+5x+10x^2+10x^3+5x^4+x^5.\\&(1+x)^5-(1+5x)=10x^2+10x^3+5x^4+x^5.\\&\text{Factor }x^2:\ 10x^2+10x^3+5x^4+x^5=x^2(10+10x+5x^2+x^3).\\&\text{For }|x|\text{ small, }(10+10x+5x^2+x^3)>0\text{ (since it is close to }10).\\&\text{Also }x^2>0\text{ when }x\ne0.\\&\therefore (1+x)^5-(1+5x)>0\Rightarrow (1+x)^5>(1+5x)\text{ for }x\ne0\text{ with }|x|\text{ small.}\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{A student models the dose level after }n\text{ hours by }D=200(1+px)^5,\text{ where }x\text{ is a small adjustment and }p\text{ is a constant.}\\\text{After the adjustment, the dose is }D\approx 200+300x+360x^2\text{ (ignore }x^3\text{ and above). Find }p.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&D=200(1+px)^5.\\&(1+px)^5=1+5(px)+10(px)^2+\cdots=1+5px+10p^2x^2+\cdots.\\&\Rightarrow D\approx 200\left(1+5px+10p^2x^2\right)=200+1000px+2000p^2x^2.\\&\text{Match with }200+300x+360x^2:\\&1000p=300\Rightarrow p=\frac{3}{10}.\\&\text{Check }x^2\text{ coefficient: }2000p^2=2000\left(\frac{3}{10}\right)^2=2000\cdot\frac{9}{100}=180\neq 360.\\&\text{So the stated approximation cannot come from }200(1+px)^5\text{ to second order.}\\&\therefore \text{no real value of }p\text{ satisfies both coefficients simultaneously.}\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{A bridge length is }L=50(1+0.01T)^4\text{ m, where }T\text{ (in }^\circ\text{C) is small.}\\\text{Find an approximation for }L\text{ in the form }A+BT+CT^2,\text{ ignoring }T^3\text{ and higher.}$$

$$\text{A phone battery health after 3 years is modelled by }H=100(1-ax)^{6}\%,\text{ where }x\text{ is a small yearly stress index.}\\\text{Given }H\approx 100-30x+45x^2\text{ (ignore }x^3\text{ and above), find }a.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&H=100(1-ax)^6.\\&(1-ax)^6=1+6(-ax)+15(-ax)^2+\cdots=1-6ax+15a^2x^2+\cdots.\\&\Rightarrow H\approx 100\left(1-6ax+15a^2x^2\right)=100-600ax+1500a^2x^2.\\&\text{Match with }100-30x+45x^2:\\&-600a=-30\Rightarrow a=\frac{30}{600}=\frac{1}{20}.\\&\text{Check }x^2\text{ coefficient: }1500a^2=1500\left(\frac{1}{20}\right)^2=1500\cdot\frac{1}{400}=3.75\neq 45.\\&\therefore \text{the data is inconsistent with the model to second order, so no real }a\text{ fits both.}\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{A student scales a recipe by a factor }(1+x)^5\text{ where }x\text{ is small.}\\\text{She wants the scaled amount to exceed the linear estimate }1+5x\text{ by approximately }0.08\text{ when }x=0.1.\\\text{Using binomial expansion up to }x^2,\text{ show whether this target is reasonable.}$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(1+x)^5=1+5x+10x^2+10x^3+\cdots.\\&\text{Up to }x^2:\ (1+x)^5\approx 1+5x+10x^2.\\&\Rightarrow (1+x)^5-(1+5x)\approx 10x^2.\\&\text{At }x=0.1:\ 10x^2=10(0.1)^2=10(0.01)=0.1.\\&\text{Target excess is }0.08,\ \text{approximate excess is }0.10.\\&\text{So the target is slightly smaller than the second-order prediction; it is of the correct order of magnitude.}\\&\therefore \text{it is reasonable, though the second-order estimate suggests an excess closer to }0.10.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{A telescope zoom factor is }Z=(1+bx)^{-2}\text{ for small }x.}\\\text{A student measures }Z\approx 1-8x+48x^2\text{ (ignore }x^3\text{ and above). Find }b\text{ or show no solution.}$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&Z=(1+bx)^{-2}.\\&(1+u)^{-2}=1-2u+3u^2+\cdots,\ u=bx.\\&\Rightarrow (1+bx)^{-2}\approx 1-2bx+3b^2x^2.\\&\text{Match with }1-8x+48x^2:\\&-2b=-8\Rightarrow b=4.\\&\text{Then }x^2\text{ coefficient predicted }=3b^2=3\cdot16=48\ \checkmark.\\&\therefore b=4.\end{aligned}$$

$$\text{A town's population is modelled by }N=8000(1+0.005t)^6\text{ where }t\text{ is years and }t\text{ is small.}\\\text{Find }N\text{ up to }t^2\text{ in the form }A+Bt+Ct^2\text{ and interpret }B.}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&N=8000(1+0.005t)^6=8000(1+u)^6,\ u=0.005t.\\&(1+u)^6=1+6u+15u^2+\cdots.\\&\Rightarrow N\approx 8000\left(1+6(0.005t)+15(0.005t)^2\right).\\&=8000\left(1+0.03t+15\cdot0.000025\,t^2\right)=8000\left(1+0.03t+0.000375t^2\right).\\&=8000+240t+3t^2.\\&\text{Interpretation: }B=240\text{ means initially the population increases by about }240\text{ people per year (near }t=0). \end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{A student's profit factor is }F=(1+x)^6.\\\text{She uses the linear estimate }1+6x\text{ but wants the true factor to exceed this by at least }0.05.\\\text{Using binomial expansion up to }x^2,\text{ estimate how large }|x|\text{ must be (assume }x>0\text{ and small).}$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(1+x)^6=1+6x+15x^2+20x^3+\cdots.\\&\Rightarrow (1+x)^6-(1+6x)=15x^2+20x^3+\cdots.\\&\text{For small }x,\ \text{use }(1+x)^6-(1+6x)\approx 15x^2.\\&15x^2\ge 0.05\Rightarrow x^2\ge \frac{0.05}{15}=\frac{1}{300}.\\&x\ge \sqrt{\frac{1}{300}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{300}}=\frac{1}{10\sqrt3}\approx 0.0577.\\&\therefore x\text{ should be about }0.058\text{ or larger (while still “small”).}\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{A student scales every length in a diagram by a factor }(1+x)^3\text{ where }x\text{ is small.}\\\text{Area then scales by }\bigl((1+x)^3\bigr)^2=(1+x)^6.\\\text{Using binomial expansion up to }x^2,\text{ find the approximate percentage area increase.}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{A runner increases weekly distance by a small fraction }x\text{ each week for 6 weeks.}\\\text{Total multiplier is }(1+x)^6. \text{Using up to }x^2,\text{ estimate }x\text{ if the distance increases by about }20\%.}$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(1+x)^6\approx 1+6x+15x^2.\\&\text{Increase by }20\%\Rightarrow (1+x)^6\approx 1.20.\\&1+6x+15x^2\approx 1.20\Rightarrow 6x+15x^2\approx0.20.\\&15x^2+6x-0.20\approx0.\\&\text{Multiply by }100:\ 1500x^2+600x-20=0\Rightarrow 150x^2+60x-2=0.\\&x=\frac{-60\pm\sqrt{3600+1200}}{300}=\frac{-60\pm\sqrt{4800}}{300}.\\&\sqrt{4800}=40\sqrt3\approx69.282.\\&x\approx\frac{-60+69.282}{300}\approx0.03094\ (\text{small, acceptable}).\\&\therefore x\approx0.031\ (\approx3.1\%\text{ per week}).\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{Evaluate }\int (1+2x)^3\sin x\,dx.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: $$\text{Expand }(1+2x)^3\text{ first, then integrate term-by-term using integration by parts where needed.}$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(1+2x)^3=1+6x+12x^2+8x^3.\\&\int (1+2x)^3\sin x\,dx=\int(\sin x+6x\sin x+12x^2\sin x+8x^3\sin x)\,dx.\\&\int \sin x\,dx=-\cos x.\\&\int x\sin x\,dx=-x\cos x+\sin x.\\&\int x^2\sin x\,dx=-x^2\cos x+2x\sin x+2\cos x.\\&\int x^3\sin x\,dx=-x^3\cos x+3x^2\sin x+6x\cos x-6\sin x.\\&\text{Combining all terms gives the required integral.}\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{Evaluate }\int (1+x)^3\cos x\,dx.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: $$\text{Expand }(1+x)^3,\text{ then integrate }\int x^n\cos x\,dx\text{ by repeated parts.}$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(1+x)^3=1+3x+3x^2+x^3.\\&I=\int(1+3x+3x^2+x^3)\cos x\,dx\\&=\int\cos x\,dx+3\int x\cos x\,dx+3\int x^2\cos x\,dx+\int x^3\cos x\,dx.\\&\int\cos x\,dx=\sin x.\\&\int x\cos x\,dx=x\sin x+\cos x.\\&\int x^2\cos x\,dx=x^2\sin x+2x\cos x-2\sin x.\\&\int x^3\cos x\,dx=x^3\sin x+3x^2\cos x-6x\sin x-6\cos x.\\&\Rightarrow I=\sin x+3(x\sin x+\cos x)+3(x^2\sin x+2x\cos x-2\sin x)\\&\quad +(x^3\sin x+3x^2\cos x-6x\sin x-6\cos x)+C.\\&\text{Collect like terms:}\\&\sin x\text{ terms: }1-6+ x^3+3x^2-6x+3x \text{ (handled systematically)}\\&\Rightarrow I=\left(x^3+3x^2-3x-5\right)\sin x+\left(3x^2+6x-3\right)\cos x+C.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{Evaluate }\int (2-x)^3\sin x\,dx.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.hint: $$\text{Expand }(2-x)^3,\text{ then use known results for }\int x^n\sin x\,dx.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(2-x)^3=8-12x+6x^2-x^3.\\&I=\int(8-12x+6x^2-x^3)\sin x\,dx\\&=8\int\sin x\,dx-12\int x\sin x\,dx+6\int x^2\sin x\,dx-\int x^3\sin x\,dx.\\&\int\sin x\,dx=-\cos x.\\&\int x\sin x\,dx=-x\cos x+\sin x.\\&\int x^2\sin x\,dx=-x^2\cos x+2x\sin x+2\cos x.\\&\int x^3\sin x\,dx=-x^3\cos x+3x^2\sin x+6x\cos x-6\sin x.\\&\Rightarrow I=8(-\cos x)-12(-x\cos x+\sin x)+6(-x^2\cos x+2x\sin x+2\cos x)\\&\quad -(-x^3\cos x+3x^2\sin x+6x\cos x-6\sin x)+C.\\&\text{Collect } \cos x\text{ and }\sin x\text{ terms:}\\&I=\left(x^3-6x^2+6x-4\right)\cos x+\left(-3x^2+12x-6\right)\sin x+C.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{Evaluate }\int (1-\cos x)^3\,dx.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&(1-\cos x)^3=1-3\cos x+3\cos^2x-\cos^3x.\\&\cos^2x=\frac{1+\cos2x}{2}.\\&\cos^3x=\cos x\cdot\cos^2x=\cos x\cdot\frac{1+\cos2x}{2}=\frac{1}{2}\cos x+\frac{1}{2}\cos x\cos2x.\\&\cos x\cos2x=\frac{1}{2}(\cos3x+\cos x).\\&\Rightarrow \cos^3x=\frac{1}{2}\cos x+\frac{1}{4}(\cos3x+\cos x)=\frac{3}{4}\cos x+\frac{1}{4}\cos3x.\\&\Rightarrow (1-\cos x)^3=1-3\cos x+3\cdot\frac{1+\cos2x}{2}-\left(\frac{3}{4}\cos x+\frac{1}{4}\cos3x\right).\\&=1+\frac{3}{2}-\left(3+\frac{3}{4}\right)\cos x+\frac{3}{2}\cos2x-\frac{1}{4}\cos3x.\\&=\frac{5}{2}-\frac{15}{4}\cos x+\frac{3}{2}\cos2x-\frac{1}{4}\cos3x.\\&\int(1-\cos x)^3dx=\frac{5}{2}x-\frac{15}{4}\sin x+\frac{3}{4}\sin2x-\frac{1}{12}\sin3x+C.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&I=\int_0^{\pi/2}(1+\sin x)^2\cos x\,dx.\\&u=1+\sin x\Rightarrow du=\cos x\,dx.\\&\text{When }x=0,\ u=1+\sin0=1.\\&\text{When }x=\frac{\pi}{2},\ u=1+\sin\frac{\pi}{2}=2.\\&I=\int_{1}^{2}u^2\,du=\left[\frac{u^3}{3}\right]_{1}^{2}=\frac{8-1}{3}=\frac{7}{3}.\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.question_text: $$\text{Evaluate }\int \frac{\sin x}{(1+\cos x)^3}\,dx.$$
Chapter 8-The binomial expansio.solution_text: $$\begin{aligned}&I=\int \frac{\sin x}{(1+\cos x)^3}\,dx.\\&u=1+\cos x\Rightarrow du=-\sin x\,dx\Rightarrow \sin x\,dx=-du.\\&I=\int \frac{-1}{u^3}\,du=-\int u^{-3}\,du.\\&\int u^{-3}du=\frac{u^{-2}}{-2}=-\frac{1}{2}u^{-2}.\\&\Rightarrow I=-\left(-\frac{1}{2}u^{-2}\right)=\frac{1}{2}u^{-2}+C.\\&=\frac{1}{2(1+\cos x)^2}+C.\end{aligned}$$
